themes.meaning: Listen Like a Winnowing Basket - sift helpful words from noisy distractions.
themes.belief: I keep the words that help me grow.

themes.meaning: See Clearly Like Ganesha's Eyes - notice what is true before you decide.
themes.belief: I look carefully before I decide what is true.

activity.title: Winnowing Breath
activity.hook: Can you breathe in the words that help and let the noisy ones float away?
steps: Sit comfortably and think of one helpful sentence someone said to you.
Breathe in as you whisper that helpful sentence to yourself.
Breathe out and imagine noisy unhelpful words blowing away like husks in the wind.
activity.reflection: Which words felt worth keeping today?
activity.affirmation: I keep the words that help me grow.
activity.real_life_transfer: Later today, pause for one breath before deciding which words to keep.

activity.title: Keep or Let Go Cards
activity.hook: Can you beat the noise and sort the words that help you grow?
steps: Place two labels in front of you: KEEP and LET GO.
Read or hear one word card at a time.
Put helpful growth words in KEEP and noisy put-down words in LET GO.
Pick one KEEP card to say out loud at the end.
activity.reflection: Which card would you like to remember the next time someone speaks to you?
activity.affirmation: I keep the words that help me grow.
activity.real_life_transfer: The next time you hear mixed messages, look for one sentence that truly helps you grow.

printable.title: Helpful Words / Noise
printable.child_action: Sort each card into KEEP or LET GO.

activity.title: Helpful or Noisy?
activity.hook: Can you catch the words that help you grow and spot the words that are just noise?
steps: Listen to three sentences someone says to you today, or remember three you heard recently.
After each one, ask: 'Does this help me grow, or is it just noise?'
Choose one sentence to keep and one sentence to let go.
Say your keep sentence once more so it stays louder in your mind than the noisy one.
activity.reflection: Which words were truly helpful, and which ones were only noise?
activity.affirmation: I keep the words that help me grow.
activity.real_life_transfer: Later today, when you hear mixed messages, quietly sort them into keep or let go.

activity.title: Keep the Helpful Part
activity.hook: Can you listen for the one helpful part in what someone says, even if the rest feels noisy?
materials: a pebble or small soft object
steps: One person shares a short opinion, reminder, or piece of advice while holding the pebble.
The listener waits quietly and then says one part that felt helpful.
If there was a noisy or unkind part, the listener names it as something to let go.
Switch turns and try again with a new sentence.
activity.reflection: What changed when you listened for the helpful part instead of holding onto the noisy part?
activity.affirmation: I keep the words that help me grow.
activity.real_life_transfer: At home today, try finding one useful sentence to keep, even if you do not keep the rest.

activity.title: Noise Catcher Crown
activity.hook: Can you build something that catches helpful words and lets noisy words fall away?
steps: Make a paper crown or headband strip.
On one side, write or draw three helpful words or sentences you want to keep.
On the other side, add two noisy messages you want to let fall away.
Put on the crown and point to the words you will keep before taking it off.
activity.reflection: Which helpful words do you want your mind to hear louder than the noise?
activity.affirmation: I keep the words that help me grow.
activity.real_life_transfer: Later today, remember one crown word when noisy words show up.

activity.title: Clue Pause
activity.hook: Can you pause your eyes long enough to notice one true clue before you guess?
steps: Look at one object in the room for ten quiet seconds.
Name three details you can actually see.
Only then say what you think the object tells you.
activity.reflection: What did you notice after you slowed down your looking?
activity.affirmation: I look carefully before I decide what is true.
activity.real_life_transfer: Next time you feel ready to guess quickly, pause and look for three clues first.

activity.title: Spot the Real Clue
activity.hook: Can your eyes find the clue that is true, not just the clue that is loud?
steps: Look at the picture and find all the details you can.
Circle the details that are real clues.
Cross out the details that are distracting but do not prove anything.
Explain which clue helped you decide.
activity.reflection: Which detail looked important at first but was not the best clue?
activity.affirmation: I look carefully before I decide what is true.
activity.real_life_transfer: When something seems obvious later today, ask yourself what you actually saw.

printable.title: Real Clue / Distracting Clue

content_spec.scene_prompt: A child sees a spilled juice box, wet footprints, an open window, and a sleeping cat.
content_spec.task: Circle the clues that truly help explain what happened.

printable.child_action: Circle the real clues and cross out distracting details.

activity.title: True Clue Hunt
activity.hook: Can your eyes find which detail is truly important, not just the one that grabs attention first?
steps: Look at a room, shelf, table, or outdoor spot with lots to notice.
Name three details that stand out first.
Then ask which one actually helps you understand what is happening there.
Choose the truest clue and explain why the other details were less important.
activity.reflection: Which clue turned out to be truly important, and which ones were only eye-catching?
activity.affirmation: I look carefully before I decide what is true.
activity.real_life_transfer: Later today, ask yourself which clue is actually true and important before you decide.

activity.title: See Before You Say
activity.hook: Can you separate what you saw from what you guessed before you choose what to believe?
steps: One person holds up an object or photo.
The first speaker says only what they can actually see.
The second speaker names one guess and one real visible clue.
Together, decide whether the guess matches the visible evidence or needs to change.
Choose the version that fits what is actually true.
activity.reflection: How did the visible clues change what you chose to believe?
activity.affirmation: I look carefully before I decide what is true.
activity.real_life_transfer: When you react fast later today, pause and ask what you really saw before choosing your answer.

activity.title: Choose the Truest Picture
activity.hook: Can you make two quick pictures and choose the one that shows what is really true?
steps: Think of a small moment, like a messy table, a frowning face, or spilled water.
Draw a first quick picture showing the first guess your eyes might make.
Draw a second picture showing what might be more true after you look for better clues.
Circle the picture you believe is truer and say which clue helped you choose it.
activity.reflection: What clue helped you choose the picture that felt truer?
activity.affirmation: I look carefully before I decide what is true.
activity.real_life_transfer: Later today, remember that your first picture is not always the truest one.
